abstract: We present a rigorous selection principle for heterotic flux compactifications in the torsional \mathrm{SU}(3) slice. In a left-invariant ansatz, the coherent-sector contraction condition (FCC) of a general fixed-point framework is shown to be equivalent to the standard anomaly/primitivity/quantization system evaluated componentwise on invariant (2,2) bases. Consequently, FCC selects discrete loci on explicit compact examples: the complex balanced Iwasawa threefold (fixing r_3) and a balanced non-integrable \text{Lens}\times\text{Nil} background (fixing R_1/R). We provide coefficient-level decompositions of dH, \mathrm{Tr}_{\mathrm{grav}}R_{+}^{2}, and \mathrm{Tr}F^{2} in invariant frames, and record a normalized cubic Yukawa on Iwasawa. These results clarify how a rigorous selection mechanism organizes heterotic flux vacua without new dynamics beyond the torsional \mathrm{SU}(3) system with R_{+}.
